transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
I'm here because I am just so distressed about my skin. I have this terrible acne and scarring all over my face, and it's honestly all I can think about lately.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time checking your skin, comparing it to others, or avoiding mirrors or social situations because of how it looks?

Yes, I do it constantly. I spend hours in front of the mirror inspecting every little mark and comparing my face to everyone I pass on the street. On bad days, I get so anxious that I avoid mirrors entirely and just stay inside because I can't bear for anyone to see me.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Body Dysmorphic Disorder, Major Depressive Disorder, Generalized Anxiety Disorder], but the interview now strongly supports Body Dysmorphic Disorder: the patient is preoccupied with perceived facial flaws, spends hours checking and comparing, and avoids mirrors/social situations due to appearance concerns. Major Depressive Disorder and Generalized Anxiety Disorder are less likely because the distress is specifically centered on appearance rather than a broader depressed mood or generalized, multi-domain worry.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient is preoccupied with perceived facial defects (acne/scarring) and spends excessive time checking, comparing, and avoiding mirrors/social situations because of appearance concerns. This pattern is most consistent with body dysmorphic disorder. OCD and major depressive disorder are less likely because the distress is specifically centered on appearance-related preoccupation and compulsive checking/avoidance.
